name: Plain Suet Dumplings
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Sift two pounds of flour into a pan, and add a salt-spoon of salt
Mince very fine one pound of beef suet, and rub it into the flour
Make it into a stiff dough with a little cold water
Roll it out an inch thick or rather more
Cut it into dumplings with the edge of a tumbler
Put them into a pot of boiling water, and let them boil an hour and a half
Send them to table hot, to eat with boiled loin of mutton, or with molasses after the meat is removed

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Sift two pounds of flour into a pan, and add a salt-spoon of salt
2. Mince very fine one pound of beef suet, and rub it into the flour
3. Make it into a stiff dough with a little cold water
4. Roll it out an inch thick or rather more
5. Cut it into dumplings with the edge of a tumbler
6. Put them into a pot of boiling water, and let them boil an hour and a half
7. Send them to table hot, to eat with boiled loin of mutton, or with molasses after the meat is removed
